policy: The only differences allowed between a reviewed spoken form and its local transcription. A transcriber writes some spoken words as symbols or digits; these rules map such a transcript token back to the words it stands for, and every application is listed in the verification record. Nothing else is equated: any other difference is a missing, added or substituted word and fails. A rule never changes scientific meaning, and passing here does not prove pronunciation - human listening remains the final gate. Add a rule only after a person has checked the audio it came from, and bump the version.

integers.form: English number words for the exact value, no 'and', hyphenated tens (96,485 = ninety-six thousand four hundred eighty-five; 1 = one; 9 = nine)
integers.observed: whisper ggml-small.en writes spoken numbers as digits ('one' -> '1', 'ten' -> '10', 'ninety-six thousand ...' -> '96,485')

spelling.policy: British and American spellings of the same scientific word are the same spoken word. Both the reviewed spoken form and the transcript are compared in the canonical spelling below; every place where either side was respelled is listed in the verification record. The authored spoken text is never changed.
spelling.observed: owner review 2026-10-03: whisper ggml-small.en writes American spellings ('millimeter') for British script spellings ('millimetre')

decimals.form: a transcript decimal such as 0.21 stands for its integer part in words, the word 'point', then every decimal digit as its own word, in order (0.21 = zero point two one). The value is kept exactly: 0.20, 0.201 or 0.12 never match 'zero point two one', and 'point twenty-one' never matches 0.21.
